sections.title: Christmas in Hungary
sections.content: The main Christmas evening in Hungary is *szenteste*, Christmas Eve, 24 December. The family decorates the tree (*karácsonyfa*) and opens the presents (*ajándék*, A1), which the *Jézuska* ("little Jesus") traditionally brings. On 6 December the *Mikulás* comes earlier and puts sweets in children's boots. *halászlé* (fish soup) is a common Christmas Eve dish, and *bejgli* is a roll with a poppy-seed or walnut filling. *karácsony* is Christmas itself, and *ünnep* is any holiday or festival. The wishes use the accusative you know from A1: *Boldog karácsonyt!* (like *Boldog születésnapot!*) and *Kellemes ünnepeket!* with the plural object ending *-ket* (A1 Unit 22).

sections.title: Key words
rows: the Christ child who brings the presents

items.spanish: A karácsonyfa alatt sok ajándék van.
items.english: Under the tree there are many presents.
On Christmas Eve we eat fish soup, and bejgli afterwards.

sections.content: *Szenteste* is the evening of 24 December, not the 25th: that is when the family gathers and the presents are opened. Like *este* ("in the evening"), *szenteste* needs no ending when it means "on Christmas Eve": *Szenteste halászlét eszünk*.
